entries.title: I Kings 5:1
segments:
Tyre; a city of the Phenicians on the Mediterranean, north of Canaan. 
 
Kings as well as subjects are bound to love one another, to rejoice in each other's prosperity, and seek each other's good.

entries.title: I Kings 5:4
segments: Peace is the gift of God.  It should be received with gratitude, and employed by rulers and people in the prosecution of such works, and such only, as will be for his glory and their highest prosperity.

entries.title: I Kings 5:6
segments:
They; the subjects of Hiram. 
 
  Zidonians; inhabitants of Zidon, a city north of Tyre.

entries.title: I Kings 5:9
segments: The difference in the climate, soil, and productions of different countries, renders an interchange of commodities a mutual benefit; and this should ever be so conducted as to benefit all concerned.

entries.title: I Kings 5:11
segments: Twenty thousand measures; in the Hebrew, twenty thousand cors, and so also below, thirty thousand men consisted of Israelites.

entries.title: I Kings 5:13
segments:
Levy out of all Israel; this levy of thirty thousand men consisted of Israelites. 
 
The building of suitable houses for public worship is essential to the highest prosperity of the community, and all should be disposed to do their part towards the accomplishments.

entries.title: I Kings 5:15
segments: Threescore and ten thousand--fourscore thousand; these one hundred and fifty thousand men were of the remnants of the Canaanites,

.  It should be borne in mind, 
 
(1) that every piece of timber had to be carried chiefly, if not entirely by hand, from Lebanon to the sea; 
 
(2) that these hewers and bearers prepared and collected timber not only for the temple, but also for Solomon's own house, and for many other sumptuous edifices which he was engaged in building. 
 
See
.  It is reasonable to suppose that a portion of them were employed in hewing and transporting stones also, as well as timber.

entries.title: I Kings 5:16
segments: Three thousand and three hundred; the number of chief officers set over the one hundred and fifty thousand men is here stated at three thousand three hundred; while in
, the chief officers over Solomon's work are given as five hundred and fifty.  The sum of these two numbers is three thousand eight hundred and fifty.  In
, the chief officers set over the one hundred and fifty thousand are stated at three thousand six hundred; while in

, the chief officers that bare rule over the people are given as two hundred and fifty.  These two numbers again make three thousand eight hundred and fifty.  It is evident that the apparent discrepancy between the two accounts, in Kings and Chronicles, arises simply from different modes of classifying these officers.

entries.title: I Kings 5:18
segments: Stone-squarers; in the margin, Giblites; inhabitants of Gebal a town near Zidon.
